replication.target_description: Candidate report explicitly identifies its exact replication of Trafimow and Hughes (2012), Study 3: random-effects meta-analysis of word-generation death-thought accessibility, death/no delay versus all other conditions (death/delay and both dental-pain conditions). Matched by study and experimental comparison; bibliographic/version identity remains unverified.

n.sample_role: Analytic participants in the exact-replication word-generation meta-analysis, unresolved; labs are separate meta-analytic units.
n.exclusions: Participant exclusions: awareness of TMT/study purpose, not following instructions, incomplete tasks, or completion under five minutes. METAlab additionally excluded from this analysis for insufficient cases. Overall counts pool two randomly assigned outcome tasks.
n.location: Results > Primary Analyses, opening paragraphs; Discussion opening paragraph
n.quote: A total of 22 labs 40 collected data from a total of 4,641 participants (3,415 after select participants were excluded -see above). ... One lab, METAlab, had to be excluded from this analysis due to an insufficient number of cases in one of the conditions. ... Across 22 labs, using data from 3,447 participants, we examined the extent to which death thought accessibility after a mortality salience induction is dependent on the passage of time.

notes: IDENTITY: The supplied canonical text opens with 'Registered Replication Report: Study 3 from Trafimow and Hughes (2012)'. Its content is a completed primary replication report rather than a preregistration or secondary summary. However, no replication author byline or replication DOI appears in the supplied parse. The neutral replication reference is only WITHDRAWN (2024), DOI 10.31234/osf.io/esu9z. Exact author/DOI/version identity cannot be fully authenticated using permitted files; positive ES is confidence false pending independent parent review. No PDF supplied; page 21 cannot be verified. The parse contains incomplete lab tables and figure captions without forest-plot values. TARGET: Table 2 explicitly names the exact Study 3 replication as word generation, Death/no delay versus All other conditions, distinguishing it from delay-only tests, word-fragment outcomes, continuous-delay regression and heterogeneity tests. DIRECTION: Preserve printed .08 and results-paragraph direction literally; Discussion says no-delay participants produced more words, opposite the quoted results paragraph. No sign correction made. N: 4,641 recruited, 3,415 overall post-exclusion, and 3,447 Discussion participants are candidate overall totals, not established target analytic N. Outcome assignment splits participants and METAlab is additionally excluded. No explicit mutually exclusive final target group counts permit summation.
